title: The Story of 1st Lt. James O. Conway
description:
The story of 1st Lt. James Conway is retold for Veterans Day and on the 60th anniversary of his death on November 12, 2014. 

While intercepting an aircraft as part of the 101st Fighter Interceptor Squadron, Lt. Conway’s plane malfunctioned shortly after takeoff from Logan Airport in Boston Massachusetts.  Rather than ejecting, Lt. Conway stayed with the aircraft and guided it away from crowded residential areas.

This 102nd Intelligence Wing video is a combination of historic footage, stock footage, and location shots in East Boston.

transcript.text: - [Announcer] This Veterans Day there
are approximately 8500 men and women actively serving
in the Massachusets National Guard.
For more than 377 years Massachusets National Guard
members have served in every major armed conflict
with each veterans service telling it's own story.
One of those stories is of First Lieutenant James Conway
a pilot from the 102nd Fighter Interceptor Wing
who's choice likely saved
the lives of many East Boston residents.
Long before the 102nd became an intelligence wing
and before they moved to Otis Air National Guard Base,
they were the 102nd Fighter Interceptor Wing,
stationed at Logan Airport in Boston.
At the height of the cold war the wing was tasked
with protecting the Northeastern United States
from aerial threats.
On October 2nd 1954 Lieutenant Conway was one
of two alert pilots on duty.
They're job was to respond to any aerial threat.
In the late morning on that warm fall Saturday
the pilots were ordered to intercept an unknown aircraft.
Within minutes Lieutenant Conway
and his F94 Starfire jet were speeding down the runway.
- Shortly after takeoff
his single engine F94 Starfire lost power.
Instead of ejecting from his disabled aircraft
and saving himself Lieutenant Conway chose
to make the ultimate sacrifice.
- [Announcer] Loaded with ammunition and fuel
the jet was losing altitude quickly
and heading directly for a residential area in East Boston.
- Lieutenant Conway nosed the aircraft down into
the embankment along Bayswater Avenue.
This sacrifice, while killing him instantaneously,
saved the lives of countless families
and future generations of East Boston citizens.
- I had a month old baby in the crib
and all of a sudden, I was in my kitchen and boom!
This terrible, terrible explosion.
And I picked the baby up and ran outside
and all black smoke was down the street.
If he'd gone left or right he would've killed many people
but he just, what he did was a very brave thing.
- Today if you drive down Bayswater Street East Boston,
you can see Lieutenant Conway's memorial plaque
with an inscription detailing his sacrifice.
His story has become part of the heritage
of the 102nd intelligence wing.
It's one of a countless number of stories
from veterans of the Massachusets National Guard
and the United States Military.
For Otis Air National Guard base,
I'm Master Sergeant Aaron Smith.
